Recorded in the X.0 format. The owner gave these on 2026-11-12; the integrator relayed them to the lanes. None of them
creates a new ADR number: each one applies an existing ADR or requirement.

| Topic | Decision | Status | Consequences |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Job side data** | Data that Sangam keeps about engine jobs lives in **Sangam side tables**, not in new columns of Operaton's tables | **DECIDED** by the owner | Applies ADR-D-16 (Operaton as a dependency, no engine schema change). Example in tree: the partitioned-executor tables `EXEC_*` (M-056, changesets `0039-*`) |
| **Model code in the engine (SL-160, threat model TM-10)** | An **allow-list at deploy**: only reviewed delegate classes and expression functions (Sangam's own plus tenant-approved) are deployable; anything else is refused at deploy with a clear error, and external code runs as external workers | **DECIDED** by the owner; delivery OPEN (SL-160, evidence first on the existing models and packs) | Extends the ADR-D-8 rule "no scripts in the engine" to Java delegates and expressions. Today `SangamBpmnParseListener` refuses only script tasks |
| **Embedded starter (M-014)** | A plain jar plus a classifier; the core modules are on and the domain modules opt-in; the defaults are shipped; JDBC drivers are excluded (the host brings its own) | **DECIDED** by the owner; delivery in Wave 2 (W2-A) | The starter module is not in the reactor yet (`sangam/pom.xml`, 2026-11-12). | **Deliveries without a publisher (SL-146)** | Events go **through subscriptions**, not to a fixed outbox destination: they reach the destinations subscribed to their type, and nothing is written when nobody subscribes | **DECIDED** by the owner; coded (`SlaService` writes to an `EventSink`; `RegistryPortBridges` fallback) | The fixed destinations `notifications` and `sangam.registry.events`, which had no publisher, are no longer written |
